list_workspaces.title: List accessible companies
list_workspaces.purpose: Find the company workspaces currently available to the signed-in identity.
list_workspaces.useWhen: Start here, then pass a returned workspaceId to company-specific tools.
effects: Reads company names and IDs. It does not create membership or change company access.
limitations: Current identity, company access and any existing designated platform authority determine the result; OAuth scope alone adds no access.
This MCP result has a workspaces array and no REST page wrapper or pagination parameters.
list_workspaces.retry: Use bounded retries for temporary read failures. If authorization fails, refresh once when appropriate or reconnect. Check result.isError even when HTTP status is 200.

list_connections.title: List connections
list_connections.purpose: Read permitted saved connections, identity-verification evidence and worker availability for one company.
list_connections.useWhen: Find a connectionId and inspect its saved state before starting or reviewing verification.
effects: Reads permitted connection information and runtime status. It does not connect a provider or run a verification job.
limitations: Requires current company access and effective service read rights for each returned connection and environment.
Configured, hasCredential and an online worker do not prove completed provider access. Read the verification state and timestamps.
Registered and managed connections can have different optional fields. Credential values are not returned.
The MCP result includes connections and runtime, with no REST page wrapper. The current runtime does not claim verified unattended operation.
list_connections.retry: Use bounded retries for temporary read failures. If authorization fails, refresh once when appropriate or reconnect. Check result.isError even when HTTP status is 200.

list_portals.title: List assigned portals
list_portals.purpose: Find the portals the current user may access within a company.
list_portals.useWhen: Choose an accessible portal before creating a task.
effects: Reads portal names, descriptions and the current user’s portal capabilities.
limitations: Current company and portal assignments apply. Company administrators can access their company’s portals.
canCreateTask and canManage describe current OrcheSphere rights; they do not grant provider access.
This MCP result has a portals array and no REST page wrapper or pagination parameters.
list_portals.retry: Use bounded retries for temporary read failures. If authorization fails, refresh once when appropriate or reconnect. Check result.isError even when HTTP status is 200.

portals.name: Operations
portals.description: Review connection checks and requested work.

list_tasks.title: List accessible tasks
list_tasks.purpose: Read saved tasks visible to the current user in one company.
list_tasks.useWhen: Find a taskId, review work status or reconcile a task change after an uncertain response.
effects: Reads saved task details and the current user’s task role and edit capabilities.
limitations: Requires company access, parent-portal access and task assignment, unless current company or portal administrator rights apply.
Saved tasks describe requested work. Their status is not evidence that an external system executed anything.
This MCP result has a tasks array and no REST page wrapper or pagination parameters.
list_tasks.retry: Use bounded retries for temporary read failures. If authorization fails, refresh once when appropriate or reconnect. Check result.isError even when HTTP status is 200.

create_task.title: Create a task
create_task.purpose: Save requested work in an accessible company portal.
create_task.useWhen: Record a task for follow-up or review in OrcheSphere.
effects: Creates a saved task and an audit record. A non-administrator creator receives contributor access to that task.
Does not execute provider actions, run a coding agent or automatically assign the task to another user.
limitations: Requires orchesphere.jobs in addition to read, and current portal operator or administrator rights.
Providing assigneeEmail additionally requires the designated access administrator. The assignee must be an eligible active company and portal member.
The trimmed title must contain at least two characters and fit the advertised 240-character limit; description is limited to 6000 characters.
Task creation has no idempotency key or automatic deduplication guarantee.
create_task.retry: After a lost response, use list_tasks to check whether the task was saved before creating it again. Do not blindly retry task creation.

update_task.title: Update a task
update_task.purpose: Change permitted fields of an existing saved task.
update_task.useWhen: Update the title, description or work status after reviewing the current task.
effects: Updates the saved task and records the change in the audit history.
Does not perform the task or modify provider business records.
limitations: Requires orchesphere.jobs in addition to read, current company and portal access, and task contributor, reviewer or administrator rights.
Reviewers may change only status. The MCP tool does not expose task reassignment.
Allowed statuses are todo, in_progress, blocked, review, done and cancelled. A task status is separate from verification-job status.
The title must remain at least two trimmed characters; advertised field-length limits apply.
update_task.retry: Read list_tasks after an uncertain response, reconcile the current fields and then apply the intended change if still needed.

list_jobs.title: List verification jobs
list_jobs.purpose: Read the latest permitted saved verification jobs for one company.
list_jobs.useWhen: Track queued work or find a jobId to inspect its result.
effects: Reads saved jobs and available cancellation/resume guidance. It does not start, cancel or resume work.
limitations: Company administrators can read company jobs. Other users need service read access and must be the requester or have jobs_read_all for the service and environment.
Returns the latest 100 permitted jobs. MCP does not return page, total, cursor or mayHaveMore metadata.
canCancel and canResume are current guidance, not a permission grant. No MCP resume_job operation exists; protected browser recovery remains in OrcheSphere.
Queued or running is not completed provider verification. Inspect status, result and errorCode.
list_jobs.retry: Use bounded retries for temporary read failures. If authorization fails, refresh once when appropriate or reconnect. Check result.isError even when HTTP status is 200.

get_job.title: Get a job result
get_job.purpose: Read one saved verification job and its recorded result.
get_job.useWhen: Poll a returned jobId until it reaches a result or needs attention.
effects: Reads job status, attempts, timestamps and the sanitized provider-identity result when available.
limitations: Requires current service read access and requester rights or jobs_read_all, with company-administrator rights applied by the server.
A successful verification result identifies the observed account and company. It does not contain provider orders, payments, inventory or other business records.
Results and completion timestamps can be null while work is pending or unsuccessful. This result does not add the list_jobs cancellation/resume fields.
Saved verification evidence reflects its observedAt time and is not a guarantee of permanent provider access.
get_job.retry: Use bounded retries for temporary read failures. If authorization fails, refresh once when appropriate or reconnect. Check result.isError even when HTTP status is 200.

verify_connection.title: Verify a connection
verify_connection.purpose: Queue a durable read-only check that the provider credentials reach the expected account.
verify_connection.useWhen: Confirm the identity behind an existing connection and follow the returned jobId.
effects: Saves a verification job and audit record. The worker can continue processing after the requesting chat closes.
The provider operation reads account identity; a successful check updates saved identity evidence. Supported credential maintenance may renew authorization as needed.
limitations: Requires orchesphere.jobs in addition to read and current service verify rights for the connection environment.
The connection needs a supported identity-verification adapter and applicable company access/allowances. A directory entry alone is insufficient.
idempotencyKey must contain 8–100 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. The key is scoped to the current requester and company.
Returning a queued job is not completed provider access. Read get_job and do not infer that provider business-record access is implemented.
At most 30 new company jobs may be admitted in one minute; other allowances may apply. A returned job can later need provider sign-in or permission correction.
verify_connection.retry: Reuse the same idempotencyKey only for the same connection submission. Reuse with another connection fails; do not generate a new key merely because the response was lost. Read the returned job to follow progress.

cancel_job.title: Cancel a verification job
cancel_job.purpose: Cancel permitted pending or running verification work in OrcheSphere.
cancel_job.useWhen: Stop a queued, retrying, running or blocked job that is no longer needed.
effects: Marks an eligible saved job cancelled, invalidates its worker lease and records the cancellation request.
Does not undo a provider read or a result that already completed.
limitations: Requires orchesphere.jobs in addition to read. Company administrators may cancel; other callers must be non-viewers with service read access and either requester rights or jobs_cancel_all.
Terminal jobs are not rewritten. The acknowledgment is {ok:true}, not a refreshed job object.
Cancellation does not revoke the provider connection or the application’s OAuth grant.
cancel_job.retry: Read get_job after an uncertain cancellation response. Confirm the current job state before repeating.

configure_connection.title: Configure a connection
configure_connection.purpose: Register or replace the expected account and authentication configuration for a company provider connection.
configure_connection.useWhen: Save a connection after the authorized account details and credential reference are known.
effects: Saves configuration for the company, provider and environment. A changed configuration increments its version and clears previous identity-verification evidence.
An unchanged configuration may return reused:true. Saving configuration does not call provider business-record APIs or prove the connection works.
limitations: Requires orchesphere.manage in addition to read and effective service configure rights. Browser-session mode additionally requires company-administrator rights.
Provider and authMode must be a supported combination. Account ID and company name must be nonempty and at most 160 characters each.
credentialRef is an authorized credential reference, never a password, API token or secret value. Omitting it preserves a same-mode existing reference; an explicit empty string can clear it.

Browser credentials must be entered in protected provider sign-in, and browser_session rejects credentialRef. Disconnect a saved browser session before changing its pinned account or authentication mode.
Production allowances can apply. The synthetic example intentionally has no credential and returns configured, not verified.
configure_connection.retry: Read list_connections after an uncertain response and compare the current configuration before repeating a change. Do not assume replacement is harmless merely because the request looks identical.

set_service_permissions.title: Set connection permissions
set_service_permissions.purpose: Replace an assigned company member’s OrcheSphere rights for one provider and environment.
set_service_permissions.useWhen: An authorized access administrator needs to set or remove service-specific access.
effects: Replaces that member’s saved service grant and records the permission change.
Changes OrcheSphere authorization only. It does not edit the provider account’s API role or increase what its credentials permit.
limitations: Requires orchesphere.manage in addition to read and designated global access-administrator authority. Company-admin status or scope approval alone is insufficient.
The target must be an assigned company member. An exact production/sandbox grant overrides the all-environments default; an empty actions array denies that grant’s access.
Nonempty actions must include read. jobs_cancel_all also requires jobs_read_all. Viewers can receive read-only rights only.
Supported rights are read, verify, configure, jobs_read_all and jobs_cancel_all. This is not a universal provider business-record read/write role mapping.
set_service_permissions.retry: Review the member’s current permissions in OrcheSphere after an uncertain response before repeating a replacement.

set_platform_role.title: Revoke platform authority
set_platform_role.purpose: Revoke an existing platform authority assignment through the restricted internal MCP flow.
set_platform_role.useWhen: An existing designated platform administrator must remove a platform authority assignment.
effects: Revokes the existing assignment and records the authority change. The only accepted role value is none.
limitations: Internal authority only: requires orchesphere.admin in addition to read and current platform-administrator authority. Registered developer applications cannot request this scope or use this tool.
Cannot create or transfer global authority, and cannot remove the last active platform administrator.
This tool has no public REST equivalent and does not grant or revoke ordinary client-company memberships.
The example is a fictional internal-administration shape, not an operation available to registered developer applications.
set_platform_role.retry: Review current platform authority in the authorized administration interface before repeating an uncertain revocation. Do not retry a protected last-administrator failure.

protocol.title: Discover REST authorization
protocol.purpose: Discover the exact REST resource, its authorization server and supported resource scopes.
protocol.input: No body or query parameters. HEAD is also supported for metadata headers.
protocol.result: JSON resource=https://api.orchesphere.ai; authorization_servers=[https://orchesphere.ai]; scopes_supported contains orchesphere.read, orchesphere.jobs and orchesphere.manage; bearer_methods_supported=[header]; resource_name=OrcheSphere API.
limitations: The resource string has no /v1 path or trailing slash. A token bound to the MCP resource is rejected by REST.
offline_access is requested at authorization to obtain refresh tokens; it is not a REST operation scope.
Browser cross-origin API calls are not enabled. Use a backend or native client.

protocol.title: Discover MCP authorization
protocol.purpose: Discover the exact MCP resource, authorization server and resource scopes.
protocol.result: JSON resource=https://orchesphere.ai/mcp; authorization_servers=[https://orchesphere.ai]; scopes_supported contains orchesphere.read, orchesphere.jobs, orchesphere.manage and orchesphere.admin; bearer_methods_supported=[header]; resource_name=OrcheSphere.
limitations: orchesphere.admin is reserved for the existing internal authority flow; registered developer applications cannot request it.
REST and MCP tokens are resource-bound and cannot be substituted for each other.
A discovery response means authorization is available; it does not prove that an AI client or provider is connected.

protocol.title: Discover the authorization server
protocol.purpose: Find the issuer, OAuth endpoints and supported authorization behavior.
protocol.result: JSON issuer=https://orchesphere.ai with authorization_endpoint=/oauth/authorize, token_endpoint=/oauth/token and revocation_endpoint=/oauth/revoke on that issuer; code response type; authorization_code and refresh_token grant types; S256 PKCE; public-client authentication method none; supported scopes and authorization-response issuer support.
limitations: The server advertises official client metadata-document support as well as registered applications; this is not unrestricted URL-based client registration.
No public dynamic-registration or JWKS endpoint is advertised. Register an application through signed-in API & developers.
Metadata may include an internal scope unavailable to registered developer applications.

protocol.title: Authorize an application
protocol.purpose: Let a signed-in user review and approve an application’s resource and scopes using Authorization Code with S256 PKCE.
protocol.authentication: The user completes OrcheSphere browser sign-in, current account-security requirements and explicit consent.
protocol.input: Browser query: response_type=code, registered client_id, exact redirect_uri, explicit resource, requested scope, fresh random state, code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. Keep the original verifier in the client’s one-use pending authorization record.
protocol.result: The browser shows sign-in or consent. On approval, the registered callback receives code, the original state and iss=https://orchesphere.ai. On denial, it receives error=access_denied, state and iss. The authorization code expires after 120 seconds.
limitations: The exact resource is https://api.orchesphere.ai for REST or https://orchesphere.ai/mcp for MCP. Scope approval grants no company membership.
Registered applications must use an exact registered HTTPS or HTTP loopback-IP callback, including the port. Official Codex metadata-based callbacks have a separate ephemeral-loopback-port rule.
The authorization request is not a client-credentials grant or a JSON API. The server-generated consent form is browser-session-bound; third-party clients must not call it directly.
Validate state, issuer, callback path and a fresh pending record before exchanging a code. Reject duplicate or reused callback parameters.

protocol.title: Exchange or refresh tokens
protocol.purpose: Exchange a one-use authorization code for an access token, or rotate tokens for an existing offline authorization.
protocol.authentication: Public client with client_id and PKCE for code exchange. Do not send an Authorization header, client secret or client assertion.
protocol.input: application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Code exchange: grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, code, exact redirect_uri, exact resource and original code_verifier. Refresh: grant_type=refresh_token, client_id, exact resource and current refresh_token.
protocol.result: HTTP 200 JSON access_token, token_type, expires_in and scope. A refresh_token is returned only when offline_access was approved. Access-token lifetime is 300 seconds; refresh rotates the token pair within the original 30-day grant. Errors use OAuth error and error_description.
limitations: Forms are limited to 16KiB. Duplicate parameters and oversized field values are rejected.
Use the same exact resource during authorization, code exchange and refresh. REST tokens cannot call MCP and MCP tokens cannot call REST.
Serialize refresh requests and replace the saved pair atomically. Reusing an already-rotated refresh token revokes its grant.
Expiry, revocation, account-security changes and current company permissions still apply. offline_access is not a guarantee of unattended or permanent access.

protocol.title: Revoke an authorization
protocol.purpose: Disconnect the grant associated with an application’s access or refresh token.
protocol.authentication: Public client_id and the token to revoke. No Authorization header or client secret.
protocol.input: application/x-www-form-urlencoded with client_id and token. token_type_hint may be sent but the current implementation does not use it to select the token type.
protocol.result: Empty HTTP 200. A matching token revokes its authorization grant; an unknown token is a successful no-op. Later use of tokens from a revoked grant is rejected.
limitations: Forms are limited to 16KiB. The client must be recognized.
Revocation does not delete saved jobs/tasks or disconnect provider credentials. Already saved work remains subject to current authorization checks.
Revoking this user grant differs from revoking a registered application itself through API & developers.

protocol.title: Call the MCP interface
protocol.purpose: Initialize an MCP connection, discover permitted tools and call them with explicit company context.
protocol.authentication: Authorization: Bearer token approved for the exact resource https://orchesphere.ai/mcp.
protocol.input: JSON-RPC 2.0 with initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list or tools/call. For calls, supply params.name and params.arguments matching the tool schema. Send Content-Type: application/json.
protocol.result: initialize returns protocolVersion, tool capabilities, serverInfo and instructions; initialized notification returns empty 202; ping returns an empty result; tools/list returns scope-filtered definitions. Successful calls return result.content, result.structuredContent and isError:false. Tool/action failures commonly return HTTP 200 with isError:true.
limitations: Supported protocol versions are 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. This endpoint does not use SSE transport or a session ID.
The JSON request body is limited to 24,000 bytes; batches are not supported. A malformed or oversized request produces the current generic parse-error response.
Missing/invalid authorization produces HTTP 401. Insufficient tool scope produces HTTP 403 with WWW-Authenticate. Inspect isError even when HTTP is 200.
Tools/list reflects approved OAuth scopes, not proof of authority for a particular company. Every call still checks current identity and company/service/portal permissions.
The ordinary MCP list payloads do not carry REST pagination metadata. Job lists return the latest 100 permitted jobs. No separate outputSchema is advertised by these tool definitions.

coverage.examples: All identifiers, accounts, people and timestamps in these examples are fictional. Replace them with values returned for the consenting user. Examples are not live receipts.
coverage.mcpResultFormat: exampleArguments is the tools/call arguments object. exampleResult is the successful structuredContent payload, also JSON-encoded in text content; it is not the enclosing JSON-RPC response. No separate runtime outputSchema is claimed.
boundaries: Only the API companion is public. Browser/session APIs, provider callbacks and private application source are outside this developer endpoint catalog.
Provider directory entries are not equivalent to implemented adapters or verified company connections.

Current public operations cover saved company information, task coordination, connection configuration/access and provider-identity verification. No provider business-record read/write API is enabled.
Service rights control OrcheSphere operations and never expand the native provider credentials’ rights.
coverage.updatePolicy: Review endpoint/tool/protocol documentation with every contract change. Release checks should compare the actual private runtime definitions with the approved public contract, validate examples and links, and require a changelog/reviewed-version update before publication.
